notes:
Inbound via self-serve signup + usage spike on trial keys. Founder CTO (Jae Kim) pinged AE in-app. Short summary:
- Product: code-aware assistant that ingests full repo context (long-context windows), supports TS/JS/Python code completion, and repo search via embeddings.
- Primary ask: Hosted API (public cloud) for fast time-to-value and no infra ops. Interested in SDKs (TypeScript first; Python later).
- Perf targets: 100-200ms for 1-2 token completions; ~800ms-1.2s for 1k-4k token generation with repo context. Throughput: peak 25 reqs/s during active dev sessions.
- Cost sensitivity: SMB startup; trying to keep monthly inference spend under $2k-$3k during early traction. Wants tips on batching + cache to stay under budget.
- Rate limits: worried about per-user burst limits causing poor UX. Asked about per-api-key throttles vs per-customer. Wants flexible rate limit tiers or token-based burst allowances.
- SDK asks: simple TypeScript examples for streaming code completions, chunked context upload pattern, and resume-from-cache examples. Also asked for local dev key rotation guidance.
- Security/compliance: will eventually require SSO (SAML) and audit logs for enterprise customers; for now requests KMS-backed key option and retention controls. Provided initial security questionnaire (see Drive link).
- Recent activity/timeline:
  * 2026-02-25: self-serve signup, tried sample completions, hit rate-limit at ~120rpm, emailed support via in-app chat.
  * 2026-02-27: quick intro call (30m) — AE Aisha + SE Marco + CTO Jae. Demo of streaming SDK requested. Notes: "Latency matters more than marginal cost for dev flow".
  * 2026-03-03: sent security FAQ and pricing deck (drive links). CTO asked for example quota configs.

- Integration details: plan to use embeddings for cross-repo search (offline index + nightly embed update), and reranking candidate completions server-side. Considering local KV cache for per-session context.
- Next steps (short): SE to share TS streaming SDK snippets + recommended rate-limit profiles; run 48h perf test; review results and propose a small dedicated burst pool if needed.
- Blockers: final decision depends on showing repeatable p95 latency under 1.2s at target throughput and a workable per-user rate-limit policy. Budget approval (founder) after perf tests.
- Internal notes for Redwood: prioritize providing streaming TypeScript snippet, an example batching + prefix cache recipe, and an exportable perf report template. Also prepare a note on cost-saving Optimize toggles (auto-batching suggestions, model fallback to smaller variants for embeddings).
